intro.text: The Bible opens with God creating the heavens and the earth. Over six days God speaks and it is so, and on the seventh day God rests.

summary.text: God creates light, sky, sea and land, plants, the sun, moon and stars, creatures of sea, air and land, and finally humankind in his own image, male and female. God sees everything he has made, and it is very good.

intro.text: The serpent questions what God said to the woman in the garden of Eden. She and the man eat the fruit of the tree God told them not to eat, and everything changes.
Adam and Eve's sons bring offerings to the Lord. God accepts Abel's offering and not Cain's, and Cain's anger leads to the first murder.
The earth is filled with violence, but Noah finds grace in the eyes of the Lord. God tells him to build an ark and bring his family and the animals into it.
The whole earth has one language. People on the plain of Shinar set out to build a city and a tower reaching to heaven, to make a name for themselves.
God tells Abram to leave his country and his father's house for a land God will show him, and promises to make of him a great nation through whom all families of the earth will be blessed.

stories.title: Three visitors and promise of Isaac

intro.text: God tells Abraham to take his son Isaac, whom he loves, to a mountain in the land of Moriah and offer him there. This is one of the most searching stories in Genesis.

stories.title: Return to Bethel and Rachel's death

intro.text: Years after his brothers sold him into slavery, Joseph is ruler over Egypt. His brothers stand before him without knowing who he is, until he can no longer hold back.
Moses is keeping sheep near Horeb, the mountain of God, when he sees a bush that burns but is not consumed. God calls to him from the bush.
Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go. Ten plagues follow, from water turned to blood to the death of the firstborn. These chapters tell the first nine and the warning of the tenth.
Before the last plague, God tells each household in Israel to kill a lamb and put its blood on the doorposts, and to eat the meal ready to leave. Israel is told to keep this day as a feast for ever.
Israel has left Egypt, but Pharaoh's army pursues them to the edge of the sea. Moses tells the people to stand still and see the salvation of the Lord.

summary.text: Moses stretches out his hand, a strong east wind blows all night, and Israel crosses on dry ground. When the Egyptians follow, the waters return. The people fear the Lord and believe him and his servant Moses.

intro.text: At mount Sinai, with thunder and lightning on the mountain, God speaks the ten commandments to Israel.
While Moses is on the mountain, the people ask Aaron to make them gods. He makes a calf of gold, and Moses comes down to find them worshipping it.

stories.title: Moses intercedes and sees God's glory
Moses asks for a shepherd for Israel
Reuben and Gad settle east of Jordan

intro.text: Joshua meets the captain of the Lord's host near Jericho. Israel is told to march around the shut-up city once a day for six days, and seven times on the seventh.

stories.title: Achan's sin and defeat at Ai
Sun stands still and southern campaign
Naomi and Ruth return to Bethlehem

intro.text: Ruth, a Moabite widow, goes to glean leftover grain in the fields to provide for her mother-in-law Naomi. She happens to come to the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's late husband.
The boy Samuel serves under the priest Eli at Shiloh. One night he hears a voice calling his name, and thinks it is Eli.
The Philistine champion Goliath challenges Israel's army for forty days. David, a young shepherd bringing food to his brothers, hears the challenge.

summary.text: David refuses Saul's armour and goes out with his sling and five smooth stones, saying the battle is the Lord's. He strikes Goliath with a stone and the Philistines flee.

stories.title: David flees to Nob and Gath
David spares Saul in the cave
Saul and the medium at Endor
The death of Saul and Jonathan

intro.text: The Philistines defeat Israel on mount Gilboa. Saul's sons, Jonathan among them, are killed, and Saul himself dies. First Samuel and First Chronicles both record it; Chronicles adds why Saul died.

David brings the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem with music and dancing. On the way, Uzzah touches the ark and dies, and David waits three months before trying again. Chronicles gives the fuller account, with the Levites and their songs.
David wants to build a house for God. Through the prophet Nathan, God answers that he will build David a house instead: a lasting kingdom through David's offspring. David responds with a prayer.

David orders a count of the fighting men of Israel, and then knows he has sinned. A plague follows, which stops at the threshing floor of Araunah (called Ornan in Chronicles), where David builds an altar.
God appears to the young King Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and says, "Ask what I shall give thee." Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people.
Solomon builds the house of the Lord in Jerusalem with cedar from Lebanon and craftsmen from Tyre. Kings and Chronicles both describe the work and its furnishings in detail.
The ark is brought into the finished temple and the glory of the Lord fills the house. Solomon blesses the people and prays a long prayer of dedication.
The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon's fame and comes to test him with hard questions. She sees his wisdom and his court, and blesses the Lord his God.

After Solomon's death, the people ask his son Rehoboam to lighten their burdens. He takes the advice of the young men instead of the old, and ten tribes turn to Jeroboam. The kingdom divides into Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
After three years of drought, Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal to a contest on mount Carmel: each side will call on its god, and "the God that answereth by fire, let him be God."
Naaman, commander of the army of Syria, has leprosy. A captive Israelite girl tells of a prophet in Samaria who could heal him, and the prophet Elisha sends him to wash in the Jordan seven times.
When Athaliah seizes the throne of Judah and kills the royal heirs, the infant Joash is hidden in the temple for six years. The priest Jehoiada then crowns him king. Joash later repairs the temple.
Hezekiah, king of Judah, removes the high places and trusts in the Lord. Chronicles tells at length how he reopened and cleansed the temple and kept a great Passover.

Sennacherib, king of Assyria, sends his officers to Jerusalem to demand surrender. Hezekiah takes the threatening letter to the temple and prays, and the prophet Isaiah brings God's answer. The same events are told in Kings, Chronicles and Isaiah.

stories.title: Hezekiah's illness and the envoys from Babylon

intro.text: Hezekiah is sick to the point of death. He prays, and Isaiah tells him that fifteen years will be added to his life, with the sign of the shadow going back on the sundial. Afterwards envoys from Babylon visit, and Hezekiah shows them all his treasures.

Manasseh reigns longer than any other king of Judah and leads the people into the worship of other gods. Kings records his evil and its consequences; Chronicles adds that he was taken to Babylon in chains, humbled himself, and prayed.

stories.title: Josiah and the book of the law

intro.text: During repairs to the temple, the priest Hilkiah finds the book of the law. When it is read to King Josiah he tears his clothes, and he leads Judah in renewing the covenant and keeping the Passover.

related.note: How doth the city sit solitary

intro.text: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, besieges Jerusalem. The city falls, the temple is burned, and the people are carried away into exile. Kings and Jeremiah both record it.
Haman has obtained a decree to destroy the Jews of the Persian empire. Mordecai urges Queen Esther to go to the king, though to approach him unsummoned could cost her life.
Psalm 23, a psalm of David, pictures the Lord as a shepherd who provides, leads and comforts, and as a host who prepares a table.
In a vision, Ezekiel is set down in a valley full of very dry bones. God asks him, "Son of man, can these bones live?"

stories.title: Daniel and friends refuse royal food

intro.text: King Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image and commands everyone to bow to it. Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego refuse.
At King Belshazzar's feast, using the gold and silver vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem, the fingers of a man's hand appear and write on the wall. Daniel is called to read it.
Officials of King Darius trick him into making a law that no one may pray to any god or man but the king for thirty days. Daniel keeps praying three times a day at his open window.

summary.text: Daniel is thrown into the den of lions. In the morning the king finds him unhurt: God sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths. Darius decrees that all should fear the God of Daniel.

stories.title: Locust plague and call to repent
Judgment of Edom and restoration of Zion

intro.text: God tells the prophet Jonah to go to the great city of Nineveh and cry against it. Jonah sets off by ship in the opposite direction.

stories.title: Day of the Lord and restoration

intro.text: Matthew and Luke each tell how Jesus was born. Our editors have set their accounts side by side in time order, from the angel's visit to Mary to the wise men's journey. Each step shows one Gospel's own words; the first step lets you compare the two family lines.

summary.text: An angel tells Mary she will bear a son, and Joseph is told in a dream to take Mary as his wife. Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger. Angels announce the birth to shepherds, and wise men from the east follow a star to worship the child.

stories.title: John the Baptist prepares the way

related.note: The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness

intro.text: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judaea, calling people to repent and be baptized in the Jordan. Each Gospel links him with the "voice crying in the wilderness" of Isaiah 40.
Jesus comes to John at the Jordan to be baptized. As he comes up out of the water, the Spirit descends like a dove and a voice speaks from heaven. Three Gospels tell it; switch tabs to read each one.

related.note: Man doth not live by bread only

intro.text: After his baptism Jesus spends forty days in the wilderness and is tempted by the devil. Matthew and Luke record three temptations and Jesus' answers from Deuteronomy; Mark tells it in two verses.
Seeing the crowds, Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches his disciples. These three chapters include the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer and the parable of the wise and foolish builders.

related.note: He maketh the storm a calm

intro.text: A great storm rises while Jesus and his disciples cross the Sea of Galilee, and Jesus is asleep in the boat. Three Gospels tell what happened when they woke him.

summary.text: The disciples wake Jesus in fear. He rebukes the wind and the sea and there is a great calm. He asks them about their faith, and they ask one another what kind of man this is, that even the wind and the sea obey him.

stories.title: The man with the legion of devils

intro.text: On the far shore of the Sea of Galilee Jesus meets a man (two men in Matthew's account) possessed by many devils, who lives among the tombs. The devils call themselves Legion. KJV "devils" are evil spirits.

stories.title: Jesus heals a man sick of the palsy

intro.text: "Sick of the palsy" means paralysed. Friends bring the man to Jesus, in Mark and Luke by letting him down through the roof. Jesus first tells him his sins are forgiven, which troubles the scribes, and then tells him to rise and walk.

Jesus calls a tax collector sitting at his tax booth (the "receipt of custom"), named Matthew in Matthew's Gospel and Levi in Mark and Luke. Jesus then eats with tax collectors and "sinners", and explains why to those who object.

stories.title: Jairus's daughter and the woman who touched his garment

intro.text: Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, begs Jesus to come to his dying daughter. On the way, a woman who has been ill for twelve years touches the hem of his garment. The Gospels tell the two events woven together.
Jesus tells of a sower whose seed falls on four kinds of ground, and then explains the parable to his disciples.

This is the only miracle of Jesus told in all four Gospels. A great crowd has followed him to a remote place, and there is little food. Switch tabs to read Matthew, Mark, Luke or John; each keeps its own details.

summary.text: With five loaves and two fishes Jesus gives thanks, and the disciples hand out the food. About five thousand men, besides women and children in Matthew's account, eat and are filled, and twelve baskets of fragments are gathered up.

intro.text: After the feeding of the five thousand the disciples set out by boat while Jesus stays to pray. In the night he comes to them walking on the sea. Matthew alone tells of Peter stepping out of the boat.

stories.title: Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ

intro.text: Near Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks his disciples who people say he is, and then who they say he is. Peter answers for them.

Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain. There he is transfigured, which means his appearance is changed: his face and clothes shine with light. Moses and Elijah (Elias in the KJV) appear and talk with him.

summary.text: A bright cloud overshadows them and a voice says, "This is my beloved Son... hear ye him." The disciples fall on their faces. When they look up they see Jesus only, and he tells them to tell no one until he has risen from the dead.

stories.title: The parable of the lost sheep

related.note: I will seek that which was lost

intro.text: Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to look for one that is lost. Luke sets it among three parables about lost things told to Pharisees and scribes who complained that Jesus received sinners; Matthew sets it in teaching about "these little ones".
A man asks Jesus what he must do to have eternal life. Matthew says he was young, Luke says he was a ruler, and all three say he had great possessions.

stories.title: Blind Bartimaeus and the blind men near Jericho

intro.text: As Jesus leaves Jericho on his way to Jerusalem, blind men by the roadside cry out to him as the "son of David". Mark names one of them: Bartimaeus. Matthew tells of two men; Luke places the healing as Jesus comes near the city.

related.note: Thy King cometh unto thee, lowly, and riding upon an ass

intro.text: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a young donkey (an "ass" or "colt" in the KJV) as crowds spread garments and branches on the road and shout "Hosanna". All four Gospels tell it. Matthew and John point to Zechariah 9:9.

summary.text: The disciples bring the animal, and Jesus rides into the city while the crowds praise God. In Matthew the whole city is stirred and asks who this is; in Luke some Pharisees tell Jesus to rebuke his disciples, and he answers that if they were silent, the stones would cry out.

related.note: An house of prayer for all people
John tells of Jesus cleansing the temple at a Passover early in his ministry

intro.text: In Jerusalem Jesus drives out those who bought and sold in the temple and overturns the tables of the moneychangers, saying the house of prayer had been made a den of thieves. John tells of a temple cleansing at the start of Jesus' ministry; it is linked under related passages.

Shortly before the Passover, at Bethany, a woman pours very costly ointment on Jesus. Some object to the waste. John names her as Mary, the sister of Martha and Lazarus. Luke 7 tells of a different anointing.

related.note: Paul hands on what he received about the Lord's supper

intro.text: On the night he is betrayed, Jesus eats the Passover meal with the twelve. He says one of them will betray him, and he gives them bread and the cup. Matthew, Mark and Luke each tell it in their own words.

summary.text: Jesus takes bread, gives thanks, breaks it and gives it to the disciples, saying "this is my body", and then the cup, "my blood of the new testament". They sing a hymn and go out to the mount of Olives. In Luke, Jesus also tells Peter that he will deny him three times.

intro.text: After the supper Jesus goes with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane on the mount of Olives. He prays in great sorrow, while the disciples he asked to watch with him fall asleep.

Judas arrives with an armed crowd sent by the chief priests and identifies Jesus. A disciple strikes the high priest's servant with a sword; John names the disciple as Peter and the servant as Malchus.
While Jesus is questioned at the high priest's house, Peter waits in the courtyard. Three times he is asked whether he was with Jesus, and three times he denies it. Then the cock crows.

The chief priests bring Jesus to Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor. Pilate questions him, offers to release a prisoner for the feast, and the crowd asks for Barabbas. John's account records the longest conversation between Jesus and Pilate.

related.note: He was wounded for our transgressions
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

intro.text: Jesus is mocked by soldiers, led out to Golgotha, "the place of a skull", and crucified between two others. All four Gospels tell it, each with its own words from the cross. Read one account at a time with the tabs.

summary.text: Jesus is crucified, and a title on the cross calls him King of the Jews. Darkness covers the land in the first three Gospels. Jesus dies, and in Matthew, Mark and Luke the veil of the temple is torn in two. A centurion who sees it speaks of him as righteous or as the Son of God.

intro.text: Joseph of Arimathaea, a rich man and a disciple, asks Pilate for the body of Jesus and lays it in a new tomb cut in rock. John adds that Nicodemus brought spices. Women watch where he is laid.

related.note: He rose again the third day according to the scriptures

intro.text: Early on the first day of the week, women come to the tomb and find the stone rolled away. Each Gospel tells the morning in its own way: switch tabs to read Matthew, Mark, Luke or John.

summary.text: The tomb is empty. Angels tell the women that Jesus is risen, as he said. In Matthew the women meet Jesus on the way; in John, Mary Magdalene meets him in the garden and mistakes him for the gardener until he speaks her name.

intro.text: The eleven disciples meet the risen Jesus on a mountain in Galilee, where he sends them to make disciples of all nations.
A lawyer asks Jesus, "Who is my neighbour?" Jesus answers with a story about a man beaten by robbers, the people who pass him by, and a Samaritan who stops.
"Prodigal" means wasteful. Jesus tells of a younger son who takes his inheritance and wastes it in a far country, and of the father and elder brother he left behind.

summary.text: In need, the son comes to himself and goes home to confess. His father sees him a great way off, runs to him and celebrates his return. The elder brother is angry, and the father tells him, "this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found."

intro.text: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector in Jericho, is too short to see Jesus over the crowd, so he climbs a sycomore tree.
On the day of the resurrection two disciples walk to a village called Emmaus, talking about all that has happened. Jesus draws near and walks with them, but they do not recognise him.

On the evening of the resurrection Jesus stands among his disciples and says "Peace be unto you". He shows them his hands, and his feet in Luke and his side in John. Luke and John each record the meeting.
Jesus, his mother and his disciples are at a wedding in Cana of Galilee when the wine runs out. John calls what happens next the beginning of Jesus' miracles.
Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler of the Jews, comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him that a man must be born again to see the kingdom of God.
Tired from his journey, Jesus sits by Jacob's well in Samaria and asks a woman for a drink. Jews and Samaritans did not usually have dealings with one another.
Lazarus of Bethany, the brother of Mary and Martha, is sick, but Jesus waits two days before going to him. By the time he arrives, Lazarus has been in the grave four days.
Before the feast of the Passover, Jesus rises from supper, takes a towel and washes his disciples' feet. Peter at first refuses.
Thomas was not with the other disciples when Jesus appeared to them, and says he will not believe unless he sees and touches the wounds. Eight days later Jesus comes again.
By the Sea of Tiberias, after breakfast with his disciples, Jesus asks Peter three times, "lovest thou me?"
At the feast of Pentecost the disciples are gathered together when a sound like a rushing mighty wind fills the house, and they begin to speak in other languages. Peter then speaks to the crowd.
Saul of Tarsus is on the road to Damascus to arrest followers of Jesus when a light from heaven shines around him and a voice speaks. Saul is later known as Paul.

stories.title: Dead to sin, alive to God

intro.text: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about spiritual gifts, the church as one body with many members, and, in chapter 13, about charity, which in the KJV means love.

stories.title: Christ superior to angels and Moses
River of life and final invitation
